criteria_quotes: CPT Code 29860 - Diagnostic hip arthroscopy is generally not covered as it is not medically necessary (hip arthroscopy should only be performed with radiologically proven pathology that meets the above criteria), but if at the time of surgery the radiologically proven pathology is not found, then 29860 may be billed.

Aetna considers pelvic osteotomy (e.g., peri-acetabular osteotomy (PAO)) medically necessary for a diagnosis of acetabular dysplasia (not borderline dysplasia) for persons who fulfill all of the following criteria:

answer.submission_route: Fill out Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form (in your account at aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals) and fax or mail it. Confirm the address on your denial letter first. Online: aetna.com (Member Complaint and Appeal Form) By fax: 859-425-3379 By phone: 1-800-872-3862, or the number on your card Deadline: Usually 180 days from the denial -- but your denial letter is authoritative. Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter.
